Learn more Frequently Asked Questions Learn more Registration Q: How do I register for the program? A: The registration links will be available at the bottom of the e-posters sent through your respective Cisco Networking Academy affiliated colleges. Q: What documents should I get to register for Cisco Ideathon? A: You only need documents that prove you meet the eligibility criteria. Q: Is there a minimum CGPA cut-off? A: A CGPA of 6 and above in the last highest degree obtained. Q: Do I need to register as part of college, or can I register as an individual? A: Please register as an individual only. Q: What is the duration of the Cisco Ideathon challenge? A: The Challenge is broken into 2 phases; the first phase will be an online assessment which includes MCQ and coding for a duration of 90 minutes. The shortlisted candidates will be given problem statements and given 1 weeks' time to prepare a PowerPoint presentation as a solution. During the second phase, candidates will have to present the PowerPoint presentation prepared by them during the interview discussion. Q: Will the results of the Cisco Ideathon affect any future chances of applying to Cisco? Can I still take part in a different hiring process by Cisco? A: Regardless of the outcome, all applicants can apply to any other open positions (current or future) at Cisco. Online Assessment & Submission Details Q: What are the topics required to prepare and study for this contest? A: The challenge content is mainly based on CCNA level questions. There will also be an open book test on the latest Industry technology advancements that will be in the form of a PowerPoint presentation submission. You may come prepared accordingly. Q: What Desktop configuration and accessories are required for the online challenge? A: Desktop or laptop with Internet connectivity. Web-proctoring will be enabled all the time during the contest. If the students move out of the window, the test will auto-submit, and you can potentially lose your opportunity. Q: Can I use my phone to attempt the test? A: The test needs to be attempted only from a desktop or laptop. Q: What will happen if my desktop breaks down during testing? A: Restart the test where the test was stopped within 20 minutes. Q: Are there any guidelines for using AI as part of my preparation and participation for the program? A: At Cisco, we are committed to promoting fairness, integrity, and originality in all aspects of the program management for our early in career talent programs. We value the skills, creativity, and unique perspectives that each candidate brings. As a leader in AI, we fundamentally believe in embracing innovation ethically and responsibly. Learn more about GenAI best practices and permitted uses on our GenAI Best Practices page. Internship Q: Is this contest for internship only or is it for full-time placement as well? A: All selected candidates will be offered either a full-time job offer or a dual offer (Internship position + pre-placement full-time job offer). Q: Can you give me an idea of the kind of job I am applying for with this test? A: You will be competing for an internship as part of this program and your internship, and the subsequent offer will be in the Customer Experience and Digital Enterprise Solutions, business units of Cisco. Q: Do I need to have coding skills to apply to this program? A: Coding is an essential part of a networking engineer’s skill set and will be a plus. However, coding is not required to attempt the Ideathon. Q: What is the CTC/Stipend and other benefits if selected? A: The compensation and benefits at Cisco are highly competitive. The details will be made available to you at the time of Internship and job offer. Q: What will my job location be if I get offered a role at Cisco? A: Internship positions are based out of either Bangalore, Chennai, Gurgaon, Hyderabad, Mumbai or Pune. For further queries, please reach out to us at: support_cisco_ideathon@cisco.com A sense of mutual respect and mindfulness permeates our culture-in fact, it’s the key to our success. INTERNSHIP SCHEME Eligibility Conditions & Duration: Internship opportunity shall be extended for UG/ PG/ PhD students (a Citizen of India) pursuing from a recognized University/ Institution (India/Abroad) in the disciplines of Science/Technology or have completed within six months of the application. The duration of the Internship work will be a maximum period of 45 days. The student should possess an aggregate of a minimum of 60% or a CGPA of 6.32 on a scale of 10. 2. STUDENT PROJECT TRAINEE SCHEME Eligibility Conditions & Duration: Opportunity shall be extended for the following category of students, in offline mode, with prescribed educational eligibility as stated below: Degree Eligibility Criteria Duration Engineering (BE/ BTech) Should have completed 6 th semester Minimum 45 days ME/ MTech Should have completed 1 st semester Minimum 120 days BSc/ Diploma Only final-year students Minimum 45 days MSc The student should have completed 1 st semester Minimum 120 days PhD Scholars should have completed coursework Minimum 30 months All the students wanting to pursue academic project work in DoS/ISRO shall possess an aggregate of Min. 60% or CGPA 6.32 on a scale of 10. Other Information: The internship/ project work will be allotted based on the availability of expertise, projects, facilities, and suitability of the student’s course to the work carried out at the respective Centre/Unit. All applications received will be scrutinized by the respective Centre/ Unit as per the norms. The Project Trainees/ Interns shall not be eligible for any stipend/ remuneration/ financial assistance. The Project Trainees/ Interns shall not be eligible for accommodation facilities during their internship in DoS/ISRO Centres/Units. However, subject to availability, Centres/Units may extend Guest House/Hostel Accommodation facilities, on a chargeable basis or may provide quarters for accommodation on a sharing basis. Charges shall be collected on par with employees. The students shall be extended canteen facilities on par with regular employees. Certificate will be awarded to Project Trainees/ Interns upon satisfactory completion of their project/ internship and on submission of their assignment report and its evaluation by the concerned division heads. The Project Trainees/ Interns shall be permitted only to UNCLASSIFIED areas of DoS/ISRO labs/ establishments. The Project Trainees/ Interns shall take clearance from Centres/Units for publishing papers/reports through external agents with regard to work done in DoS/ISRO Centres/Units. Note: With respect to general guidelines, students may visit the respective Centre/Unit website. 5ghackathon: 5G Hackathon 2026 Skip to Main Content Applicant Registration Login NEW National Evaluation Result 2026 Click Here to View 5G Innovation Hackathon 2026: The 5G Innovation Hackathon 2026 aims to bring together students, startups, and professionals to develop cutting-edge solutions using 5G labs in 100 institutes across India. The Hackathon will facilitate solution development in key technology areas such as AI-driven network maintenance, IoT-enabled applications, smart healthcare, industrial automation, quantum communication, and more. The hackathon provides a collaborative platform to the stakeholders to innovate and develop prototypes/applications/solutions through access to 5G labs, mentorship from industry and academic experts during the hackathon, provision of seed funding to the shortlisted proposals, and support for commercialization. Hackathon Rules: Participants must be undergraduate/postgraduate students, startups, professionals or in their collaboration with others. Each team must submit a comprehensive proposal to any of the 5G Use case labs in 100 institutes outlining their problem statement, proposed solution, and expected impact. Each institutions shall recommend 1-5 proposals to the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) after internal screening. Proposals will go through regional and national shortlisting before progressing to prototype development. Teams will have access to labs for prototype development, and will be provided mentorship by experts. The shortlisted proposals at regional level will be provided seed funding for further development of projects. The final evaluation will be based on technical execution, scalability, market readiness, societal impact, and novelty. Winning teams will receive cash prizes and opportunities to showcase their projects on national platforms. Intellectual property rights (IPR) support will be provided for viable solutions. Call for Proposals opens: 20 March 2026 - 26 April 2026 Thematic Areas: 5G / 5G Advanced–based use cases Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for telecom technology IoT-enabled applications in sectors such as healthcare, agriculture, education, industrial automation, finance and others 5G / 5G Advanced–based applications for disaster management, RedCap user equipment, and Fixed Wireless Access (FWA). Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) and their integration with 5G / 5G Advanced systems. 5G use cases leveraging advanced network capabilities, including network slicing, Quality of Service (QoS), and other native 5G features. Telecom security solutions relevant to next-generation communication systems. Tentative Timelines i. Call for proposals opens: 20 March 2026 ii. Submission deadline: 26 April 2026 iii. National level presentations (TEC): 26 May 2026 – 19 June 2026 iv. Pragati Phase — mentor assignment & prototype development (12 weeks): 22 June 2026 – 13 September 2026 v. Physical demonstrations before TEEC: 14 September 2026 onwards vi. Winners announced: 1 October 2026 vii. Awards & showcase at India Mobile Congress 2026: October 2026 Support Details Please feel free to contact us at the email below for any support/ further information: hackathon.5g@tcil.net.in User Manual Details 1. Participant Login, Registration and Proposal Submission Download User Manual Frequently Asked Questions 1. What are the focus areas of the hackathon? The hackathon focuses on 5G / 5G Advanced–based use cases, Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for telecom technology, IoT-enabled applications in sectors such as healthcare, agriculture, education, industrial automation, finance and others, 5G / 5G Advanced–based applications for disaster management, RedCap user equipment, and Fixed Wireless Access (FWA)., Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) and their integration with 5G / 5G Advanced systems, s5G use cases leveraging advanced network capabilities, including network slicing, Quality of Service (QoS), and other native 5G features, Telecom security solutions relevant to next-generation communication systems, and quantum communication. Participants are expected to create prototypes using 5G technology. 2. Who can participate in the hackathon? The hackathon is open to: Students, Startups, Tech Professionals, Industry, R&D, and Government Organizations. Undergraduate (UG) and Postgraduate (PG) students Startups and professionals Collaboration with students, startups and professionals . 3. Will mentorship be provided? Yes, experts from academia and industry will provide mentorship throughout the hackathon. 4. What is the structure of the hackathon? The hackathon consists of four stages: Stage I: Online Proposal Submission Stage II: Shortlisting at institute, regional, and national levels Stage III: Pragati Phase — mentor assignment & prototype development (12 weeks) – 3-month development period with ₹1,00,000 funding per team Stage IV: Final Evaluation & Showcase – Winners will be selected by a Technical Expert Evaluation Committee (TEEC) 5. What are the judging criteria for the prototypes? Prototypes will be evaluated based on: Technical Execution: 40% Scalability & Market Readiness: 40% Societal & Industrial Impact: 10% Novelty: 10% 6. What are the prizes for winners? 1st Place: ₹5,00,000 Runner-up: ₹3,00,000 2nd Runner-up: ₹1,50,000 Best Idea: ₹50,000 for Best Idea & Most Innovative Prototype 7. What is the timeline for the hackathon? Call for Proposals opens: 20 March 2026 Submission deadline: 26 April 2026 National level presentations (TEC): 26 May – 19 June 2026 Pragati Phase — mentor assignment & prototype development (12 weeks): 22 June – 13 September 2026 Physical demonstrations before TEEC: 14 September 2026 onwards Winners announced: 1 October 2026 Awards & showcase at India Mobile Congress 2026: October 2026 8. Will participants receive any funding? Yes, top 25-50 selected teams will receive ₹1,00,000 each for prototype development. 9. Will participants get support for intellectual property rights (IPR)? Yes, support for IPR filing will be provided if a solution qualifies for patenting, along with ₹50,000 per team for up to 25 teams. 10. Where will the winners showcase their solutions?
